walkthroughs.body_html:
Quantities & Units in Mechanics — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Quantities & Units in Mechanics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Quantities & Units in Mechanics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A particle starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s² for 3 seconds. Final velocity is:
options: 12 m/s
7 m/s

options: v² = u² + 2as
v = u + at
s = ut + ½at²

mcqs.q: What does the gradient of a straight-line graph tell you?
options: 0.003, treating significant figures the same as decimal places.
Where the line crosses the y-axis.
How steep the line is — the change in y for each unit change in x (rise over run).
How long the line is on the page.

mcqs.q: What is 0.00307 written to 2 significant figures?
options: 0.0031 — leading zeros are not significant; the first two significant figures are 3 and 0.
0.00 — counting the first two digits after the decimal point.
How long the line is on the page.
0.003, treating significant figures the same as decimal places.
4.7, because the 8 at the end rounds the 4 up to 5, which then rounds the 6 up to 7.
4.65, because rounding to 1 dp means cutting after the second decimal.
4.6 — look at the second decimal (4), which is less than 5, so round down.
How long the line is on the page.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Velocity-time graphs”?
options: Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
For constant acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ((u+v)/2)t. Useful when a is constant.
Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Variable acceleration”?
options: If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.
Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
